```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 110,
                      eval = requireNamespace("cluster", quietly = TRUE) &&
                        requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE))
library(cpueTargeting)
library(ggplot2)
```

This vignette takes a realistic multispecies logbook from the raw records to
standardised abundance indices for two species. The logbook is simulated
with `simulate_logbook()`, so it has the problems of real data (trips that
combine two tactics, coarse and missing positions, rounding, under-reported
bycatch, a species recorded under two names, fleet turnover, a closure), but
the true tactics and the true biomass trends are known and every step can be
checked.

* **Part 1** prepares the logbook. These steps are the same for every
  species: format the data, explore the fleet, choose the species set, look
  at nominal CPUE and catch composition, and derive targeting covariates.
* **Part 2** standardises **blackspot seabream**, a deep-reef demersal
  species caught by the reef handline.
* **Part 3** standardises **dolphinfish**, a seasonal pelagic migrant caught
  by trolling.

| Step | Question | Functions | Part |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Format | Which column is what? One row per operation? | `cpue_data()`, `subset()` | 1 |
| 2. Fleet | Who fished when? Specialists or mixed vessels? | `plot_fleet()`, `vessel_summary()`, `plot_vessel_profile()`, `select_vessels()` | 1 |
| 3. Species | Which species carry the targeting signal? | `species_curve()`, `plot_species_curve()`, `select_species()` | 1 |
| 4. Nominal CPUE | What do the raw data say? | `plot_nominal()`, `plot_composition()`, `plot_cpue_map()` | 1 |
| 5. Subsetting | Which trips could catch the species? | `select_tactics()`, `stephens_maccall()` | 2, 3 |
| 6. Targeting covariates | How did fishing tactics change? | `add_targeting()`, `plot_oc()`, `plot_biplot()`, `tactic_table()`, `plot_targeting()` | 1, 2, 3 |
| 7. Models | Base, spatial, Cluster, DPC, vessel effects, season | `fit_cpue()` | 2, 3 |
| 8. Diagnostics | Which terms matter? Does the error distribution fit? | `cpue_diagnostics()`, `plot_index()`, `plot_step()`, `plot_influence()`, `plot_residuals()`, `ppc_cpue()`, `plot_effects()`, `plot_vessel_effects()` | 2, 3 |
| 9. Index | The index for the assessment | `cpue_index()`, `export_index()` | 2, 3 |

How the simulator works is described in *Setting up the logbook simulator: a
user guide*; the general guidelines in *Analysing real catch and effort data:
a step-by-step guide*.

# The logbook

```{r simulate}
sim <- simulate_logbook(seed = 1)
sp_tab <- sim$settings$species
knitr::kable(sp_tab[, c("species", "group", "habitat", "depth_mu", "price")],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

Prices favour demersal species in 2000-2007 and pelagic species in
2008-2015; from 2016 prices are neutral, the bottom longline is banned deeper
than 300 m and effort is cut. Nominal CPUE (orange) departs from the true
biomass (black) in different ways for each species:

```{r om-cpue, fig.height = 5}
sim$Plots$cpue
```

This is what an analyst receives; the tactic is not in the logbook:

```{r logbook}
head(sim$logbook, 8)
```

# Part 1. Preparing the logbook

## Step 1. Format the data

`cpue_data()` turns the logbook (long format: one row per trip and species)
into one row per operation with one column per species, merges species
synonyms, and starts a processing log.

```{r format}
x <- cpue_data(sim$logbook, year = "year", species = "species", catch = "kg",
               effort = "hours", id = "trip", vessel = "vessel",
               lon = "lon", lat = "lat", covariates = "month",
               synonyms = c("Blackspot seabream" = "Pagellus bogaraveo"))
x <- subset(x, !is.na(lon), note = "positions reported")
x
```

> **Guidelines**
>
> * Define the **operation**: the unit at which catch and effort are recorded
>   (set, haul, day or trip). Here it is the trip, and about a fifth of the
>   trips combine sets of two tactics; their catch composition is a mixture.
> * Choose an **effort** measure that scales catch (here hours fished).
> * Merge **synonyms** first (here blackspot seabream recorded under its common
>   name in some trips); they change the species set.
> * Every selection with `subset()` is written to the log (`x$log`).

## Step 2. Explore the fleet

```{r fleet, fig.height = 5}
fl <- plot_fleet(x)
fl$records
fl$vessels
fl$vessel_years
```

Vessels enter and leave over the years. Each vessel's catch profile shows how
far the fleet is split into specialists:

```{r vessel-profile, fig.height = 4}
groups <- list(demersal = sp_tab$species[sp_tab$group == "demersal"],
               pelagic = sp_tab$species[sp_tab$group == "pelagic"])
plot_vessel_profile(x, groups = groups)
head(vessel_summary(x), 8)
```

Since the data are simulated, we can label the vessels with their true type:

```{r vessel-type, fig.height = 4}
type <- tapply(sim$trips$vessel_type, sprintf("V%02d", sim$trips$vessel),
               function(z) z[1])
plot_vessel_profile(x, groups = groups, by = type)
```

> **Guidelines**
>
> * Strong **fleet turnover** confounds vessel efficiency with year; random
>   vessel effects help if vessels overlap in time.
> * **Specialists** (vessels at either end of the profile plot) target the
>   same species throughout; their targeting is absorbed by a vessel effect.
>   **Mixed vessels** switch tactics with prices; that is the targeting that
>   the catch composition has to capture.
> * An **indicator fleet** (`select_vessels()`) keeps vessels that fished
>   consistently, optionally with rules on the target species
>   (`min_years_target`, `min_share_target`). Compare the index with and
>   without the selection.

## Step 3. Choose the species set

```{r species}
plot_species_curve(x, threshold = 0.95)
targets <- c("Pagellus bogaraveo", "Coryphaena hippurus")
x <- select_species(x, threshold = 0.95, keep = targets)
x$species_labels
```

```{r groups}
# the species groups that are still in the data, for the selections below
demersal <- intersect(groups$demersal, x$species_labels)
pelagic <- intersect(groups$pelagic, x$species_labels)
```

> **Guidelines**
>
> * Rank species by **occurrence** (default) and check by weight.
> * Always **keep the species of interest**, even if rare.
> * Species characteristic of other tactics are valuable even if not
>   abundant: they let the PCA separate the tactics.

## Step 4. Nominal CPUE and catch composition

```{r nominal, fig.height = 4}
nom <- plot_nominal(x, targets)
nom$index
nom$positive
nom$distribution
```

```{r composition, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_composition(x)
plot_cpue_map(x, res = 0.5, by_period = 8)
```

Expect the catch composition to shift towards pelagic species in 2008-2015,
at the same time as the prices: a first sign of targeting.

> **Guidelines**
>
> * The **share of positive trips** and the **distribution of positive
>   CPUE** guide the choice of error distribution (Tweedie or delta).
> * Abrupt changes in composition at known changes in prices, regulations or
>   gear point to targeting; gradual drifts may be abundance.

## Step 6. Targeting covariates for the whole fleet

```{r targeting}
x <- add_targeting(x)
x$targeting$pca
plot_oc(x)
```

```{r targeting-plots, fig.height = 5}
plot_biplot(x)
tactic_table(x)
pt <- plot_targeting(x, res = 0.5)
pt$time
pt$pcs_time
pt$map_tactic
```

Check the clusters against the true tactic of each trip (not possible with
real data):

```{r truth-tactics}
truth <- sim$trips[match(x$data$trip, sim$trips$trip), ]
round(prop.table(table(cluster = x$data$FT, true_tactic = truth$tactic), 1), 2)
```

Across the whole fleet, the first axis is typically dominated by the contrast
between pelagic and demersal trips (check the loadings). For a demersal
species that contrast is mostly irrelevant: what matters is the targeting
*within* the demersal trips. The worked examples therefore start by selecting
the relevant tactics and recomputing the PCA.

> **Guidelines**
>
> * **Name the tactics** after their dominant species and check that they
>   make sense to people who know the fishery.
> * **Number of PCs**: Optimal Coordinates test, not AIC; the composition is
>   not independent of the response, so AIC selects too many PCs.
> * **Continuous or discrete?** PCs represent gradual changes and mixed trips;
>   clusters assume distinct tactics.
> * Run `add_targeting()` again **after every selection**; PCs and clusters
>   depend on the operations included (`select_tactics()` does this).

```{r helper}
# relative indices of several fits against the true biomass
compare_indices <- function(fits, true) {
  idx <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(n) {
    i <- cpue_index(fits[[n]]$fit, fits[[n]]$model)
    data.frame(year = i$year, relative = i$relative, lower = i$lower,
               upper = i$upper, index = n)
  }))
  true$true <- true$true / mean(true$true)
  ggplot(idx, aes(x = year, y = relative, colour = index, fill = index)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = true, aes(x = year, y = true), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              colour = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 3) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Relative CPUE", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
         subtitle = "black: true biomass") + theme_bw()
}
```

# Part 2. Worked example: blackspot seabream

Blackspot seabream (*Pagellus bogaraveo*) lives on deep reefs and is caught
mainly by the reef handline. Its price is high in 2000-2007; during the
pelagic boom (2008-2015) much of the fleet trolls for pelagic species
instead, and in 2016 the closure moves effort.

```{r sbr-truth}
true_sbr <- logbook_truth(sim, "Pagellus bogaraveo")
```

## Step 5. Remove the trips that could not catch seabream

`select_tactics()` keeps the clusters whose catch is at least 50% demersal
species and recomputes the PCA and clusters on the remaining trips.

```{r sbr-select}
xd <- select_tactics(x, species = demersal, min_share = 0.5)
round(xd$targeting$previous$share, 2)    # demersal share of each previous cluster
tail(xd$log, 3)
```

An alternative is the habitat-based selection of Stephens and MacCall
(2004), which predicts the presence of seabream from the other species in each
trip:

```{r sbr-sm, fig.height = 4}
sm <- stephens_maccall(x, target = "Pagellus bogaraveo")
sm
pl <- plot_stephens_maccall(sm)
pl$coefficients
pl$kept
```

> **Guidelines**
>
> * `select_tactics()`: select on a **group of species** (here all demersal
>   species), not on the target alone. Clusters come from the catch
>   composition; keeping only clusters rich in the target would select trips
>   by their catch of the target, and part of its abundance signal with them.
> * The removed clusters should be clearly different (here almost no
>   demersal catch), not borderline.
> * Stephens and MacCall: check the share kept by year (`pl$kept`); a trend
>   means the selection itself follows the targeting.
> * Compare the index with and without the selection (below).

## Step 6. Targeting covariates of the demersal trips

```{r sbr-targeting, fig.height = 5}
plot_oc(xd)
plot_biplot(xd)
tactic_table(xd)
pd <- plot_targeting(xd, res = 0.5)
pd$time
pd$pcs_time
```

The new PCs describe the targeting within the demersal fishery, e.g. reef
against sediment species and shallow against deep (check the loadings).

## Step 7. Fit the models

Terms are added in a meaningful order: year only, then space, then the
targeting covariates; all models have a random vessel effect.

```{r sbr-fit}
fit_sbr <- fit_cpue(xd, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo",
                    models = c("Base", "Base+S", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
fit_sbr
```

## Step 8. Diagnostics

### Model comparison, indices and steps

```{r sbr-diag}
cpue_diagnostics(fit_sbr)
```

```{r sbr-index, fig.height = 5}
plot_index(fit_sbr, true = true_sbr)
```

```{r sbr-step, fig.height = 8}
plot_step(fit_sbr)
```

### Influence

```{r sbr-influence}
plot_influence(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")
```

The influence of the targeting term should change over time where
targeting changed, i.e. around the start and end of the pelagic boom (2008,
2016) and the closure (2016).

### Residuals

```{r sbr-residuals, fig.height = 4}
res <- plot_residuals(fit_sbr, "DPC+S", by = "FT")
res$qq
res$year
res$by
```

### Predictive check of the error distribution

Residuals check each trip against its own predicted distribution.
`ppc_cpue()` asks whether the fitted Tweedie distribution reproduces the data
**as a whole**: it simulates 50 replicate data sets from each model (with
parameter uncertainty) and compares the share of zeros, the upper tail and the
histogram of CPUE with the observed data.

```{r sbr-ppc}
pp_sbr <- ppc_cpue(fit_sbr, models = c("Base", "DPC+S"))
pp_sbr
```

```{r sbr-ppc-plots, fig.height = 5}
pp_sbr$plots$distribution
pp_sbr$plots$zeros
pp_sbr$plots$tails
```

> **Guidelines: reading a predictive check**
>
> * **Histogram** (bars: observed, zeros leftmost; points: predicted with 95%
>   ranges): bars outside the ranges show where the error model fails, e.g.
>   too many observed zeros next to too few small catches.
> * **Zeros by year**: the year effect fixes the mean, not the zeros. A model
>   without targeting covariates gives every trip in a year the same expected
>   catch and misses the zeros in years when much of the fleet fished other
>   habitats; a good targeting term brings them inside the envelope.
> * **Upper quantiles**: observed below the envelope means the model's tail
>   is too heavy, above too light.
> * Pooled checks can hide errors that cancel across years; look at the
>   by-year plots (or `by = "FT"`).

### Effects and vessels

```{r sbr-effects, fig.height = 4}
eff <- plot_effects(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")
eff$numeric
eff$space
plot_vessel_effects(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")
```

> **Guidelines**
>
> * A targeting term that matters shows **influence that changes over time**.
> * Residuals should show **no trend by year** and no pattern by tactic.
> * The error distribution should reproduce the **zeros and the upper tail
>   by year**.
> * Compare **DPC and Cluster**; if they disagree, look at the PCs over time
>   and ask whether relative abundances may have diverged.

### Sensitivity to the data selection

```{r sbr-sensitivity, fig.height = 4}
fit_sbr_all <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo", models = "DPC+S",
                        vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
x_sm <- add_targeting(subset(x, sm$selected, note = "Stephens & MacCall, seabream"))
fit_sbr_sm <- fit_cpue(x_sm, species = "Pagellus bogaraveo", models = "DPC+S",
                       vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
compare_indices(list(`demersal tactics` = list(fit = fit_sbr, model = "DPC+S"),
                     `Stephens & MacCall` = list(fit = fit_sbr_sm, model = "DPC+S"),
                     `all trips` = list(fit = fit_sbr_all, model = "DPC+S")),
                true_sbr)
```

## Step 9. The index

```{r sbr-index-table}
idx_sbr <- cpue_index(fit_sbr, "DPC+S")
knitr::kable(idx_sbr, digits = 3)
```

```{r sbr-export, eval = FALSE}
export_index(fit_sbr, "seabream_index_DPC.csv", model = "DPC+S")
```

# Part 3. Worked example: dolphinfish

Dolphinfish (*Coryphaena hippurus*) is caught by trolling and is only present
in summer and autumn. Its price booms in 2008-2015, when much of the fleet
switches to pelagic fishing.

```{r dol-truth}
true_dol <- logbook_truth(sim, "Coryphaena hippurus")
```

## Step 5. Keep the pelagic trips

```{r dol-select}
xp <- select_tactics(x, species = pelagic, min_share = 0.5)
round(xp$targeting$previous$share, 2)
tail(xp$log, 3)
```

Outside its habitat (demersal trips) a zero says nothing about dolphinfish
abundance, and the PCA of the remaining trips can now describe the targeting
among pelagic species.

## Step 6. Targeting covariates of the pelagic trips

```{r dol-targeting, fig.height = 5}
plot_oc(xp)
plot_biplot(xp)
tactic_table(xp)
pp_t <- plot_targeting(xp, by = "month", res = 0.5)
pp_t$time
pp_t$by
```

The PCs should now separate offshore species (albacore, dolphinfish) from
coastal ones (amberjack, mackerel); check the loadings.

## Step 7. Fit the models

Month enters as a cyclic smoother in every model except `Base`; the index is
averaged over the observed months.

```{r dol-fit}
fit_dol <- fit_cpue(xp, species = "Coryphaena hippurus",
                    models = c("Base", "Covariates", "Cluster+S", "DPC+S"),
                    terms = 's(month, bs = "cc", k = 6)',
                    knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
                    vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
fit_dol
```

## Step 8. Diagnostics

### Model comparison, indices and steps

```{r dol-diag}
cpue_diagnostics(fit_dol)
```

```{r dol-index, fig.height = 5}
plot_index(fit_dol, true = true_dol)
```

```{r dol-step, fig.height = 8}
plot_step(fit_dol)
```

### Influence and residuals

```{r dol-influence}
plot_influence(fit_dol, "DPC+S")
```

```{r dol-residuals, fig.height = 4}
res_dol <- plot_residuals(fit_dol, "DPC+S", by = "month")
res_dol$qq
res_dol$year
res_dol$by
```

### Predictive check by month and by year

For a migrant the share of zeros changes strongly over the year. A model
without the seasonal term predicts the same share of zeros in every month:

```{r dol-ppc-month, fig.height = 4.5}
pp_dol_m <- ppc_cpue(fit_dol, models = c("Base", "DPC+S"), by = "month")
pp_dol_m$plots$zeros
```

```{r dol-ppc-year, fig.height = 5}
pp_dol <- ppc_cpue(fit_dol, models = c("Base", "DPC+S"), by = "year")
pp_dol
pp_dol$plots$distribution
pp_dol$plots$zeros
pp_dol$plots$tails
```

### Error distribution: Tweedie or delta-lognormal?

A delta model lets the probability of a catch and the catch rate of positive
trips change separately, e.g. when the season shortens. AIC cannot compare
a Tweedie with a delta model, but a predictive check can:

```{r dol-delta, fig.height = 5}
fit_dol_dl <- fit_cpue(xp, species = "Coryphaena hippurus", models = "DPC+S",
                       family = "delta_lognormal",
                       terms = 's(month, bs = "cc", k = 6)',
                       knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
                       vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
pp_dl <- ppc_cpue(fit_dol_dl, by = "month")
rbind(data.frame(family = "Tweedie",
                 pp_dol_m$overall[pp_dol_m$overall$model == "DPC+S", ]),
      data.frame(family = "delta-lognormal", pp_dl$overall))
pp_dl$plots$distribution
pp_dl$plots$zeros
```

### Effects and vessels

```{r dol-effects, fig.height = 4}
eff_dol <- plot_effects(fit_dol, "DPC+S")
eff_dol$numeric
plot_vessel_effects(fit_dol, "DPC+S")
```

### Sensitivity

```{r dol-sensitivity, fig.height = 4}
fit_dol_all <- fit_cpue(x, species = "Coryphaena hippurus", models = "DPC+S",
                        terms = 's(month, bs = "cc", k = 6)',
                        knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
                        vessel = TRUE, spatial_k = 40, engine = "bam")
compare_indices(list(`Tweedie, pelagic tactics` = list(fit = fit_dol, model = "DPC+S"),
                     `delta-lognormal, pelagic tactics` = list(fit = fit_dol_dl,
                                                              model = "DPC+S"),
                     `Tweedie, all trips` = list(fit = fit_dol_all, model = "DPC+S")),
                true_dol)
```

> **Guidelines: seasonal species**
>
> * Include the season (cyclic smoother) in all models except `Base`, and
>   check the zeros by month with `ppc_cpue(..., by = "month")`.
> * Keep only trips that could catch the species; outside its season or
>   habitat, zeros carry no information on abundance.
> * Choose the error distribution with predictive checks and residuals, not
>   AIC across families; report the other family as a sensitivity.
> * Seasonal availability can shift between years with temperature; in real
>   data a `month x year` interaction or a temperature covariate may be
>   needed.

## Step 9. The index

```{r dol-index-table}
idx_dol <- cpue_index(fit_dol, "DPC+S")
knitr::kable(idx_dol, digits = 3)
```

# Processing logs

Every selection step is recorded, so the final data of each index can be
reported exactly.

```{r logs}
xd$log
xp$log
```

# Reporting checklist

| Item | Blackspot seabream | Dolphinfish |
|---|---|---|
| Operation and effort | trip; hours fished | trip; hours fished |
| Data selection | positions reported; demersal tactics (`select_tactics`, >= 50% demersal catch) | positions reported; pelagic tactics (>= 50% pelagic catch) |
| Species set | 95% of occurrences, target kept | 95% of occurrences, target kept |
| Targeting | PCA of demersal trips, OC test, `n_pc + 1` clusters | PCA of pelagic trips, OC test, `n_pc + 1` clusters |
| Models | Base, Base+S, Cluster+S, DPC+S; random vessel effect; Tweedie | Base, Covariates (month), Cluster+S, DPC+S; random vessel effect; Tweedie and delta-lognormal |
| Diagnostics | model table, step, influence, residuals, predictive check (zeros by year) | as left, predictive check by month and year, family comparison |
| Sensitivity | all trips; Stephens & MacCall | all trips; delta-lognormal |
| Index | DPC+S with log SE and CV | DPC+S with log SE and CV |

# Things to try

* `logbook_settings()` lists every setting (see *Setting up the logbook
  simulator*). Change the prices, the closure, the share of two-set trips
  (`logbook$two_sets`) and how often they switch tactic
  (`logbook$switch_tactic`), the reef patches (`reef_share`, `reef_scale`), or
  the loyalty of specialists (`loyalty`), and see how each affects the
  targeting covariates and the indices.
* Compare `n_pc` and the number of clusters, and the species set
  (`select_species(..., pool_other = TRUE)`).
* Define an indicator fleet with `select_vessels(..., target = ...)` and
  compare the indices.
* Give the species diverging trends (`B_start`, `r`) and check whether the
  PCs start absorbing them.
